en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-kukkuravatā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharma Xian, Imperial Preceptor of the Court Rank of Chao-san Dafu,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master Mingjiao, under imperial decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
Furthermore, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others all came together to sit in the assembly.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"You should listen attentively; I have a dhāraṇī named Kukkuṭa."
It possesses great power and can bring about auspiciousness;
it can destroy the possession by bhūtas, malevolent planets,
and the like, and it can eliminate all diseases.
These are what are called diseases of the stomach,
diseases of cold and heat, headaches, hemicrania, coughing, vomiting,
labored breathing, and even hemorrhoids and white urine.
As well as various types of wounds and so forth.
Ānanda, it can even prolong the lives of those whose life-force is about to be severed.
For this reason, I now proclaim this for you.
Ānanda, if there should be anyone who, upon hearing this dhāraṇī,
gives rise to a firm resolve and recites, reads, and upholds it,
the beneficial merit obtained by that person will be immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī,
saying: *Tadyathā | oṃ | īrimiri | cirimi | varakūṭe śrīmatedi | kuṇale*.

*ni dāntaśataniṣṭhānte* (21) *samantakuśalane* (22) *pariṇamagacchatu svāhā* (23). At that time,
the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [entered samādhi].
He addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Wherever this dhāraṇī resides, I see no one—
whether among the devas or humans, or any of the Brahmās, Māras, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas— who would dare to transgress it."
"You should receive and uphold this and explain it to others,
so that many people may obtain great benefit.
Thus [the Buddha spoke] to Ānanda and the assembly of devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others present.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced with faith and acceptance, prostrated, and withdrew.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Kukkuṭa Dhāraṇī* as spoken by the Buddha.
